segments.t: Open KTPH001Configuration → Global Settings → MessagingKTPH002 to choose which events send desktop notifications. Changes apply to open sessions when you save. The existing choices are stored in KTPH000 and are retained when upgrading.
Desktop notification when a coding agent needs a decision or finishes while you are not looking at its pane
Desktop notification when the bell rings in a tab you are not looking at
Desktop notification when a long-running command finishes in a tab you are not looking at
Desktop notification when a program in a tab you are not looking at asks for one (OSC 9, OSC 777)
Desktop notification when an AI agent or AI swarm run in a tab you are not looking at finishes or waits for you

Under KTPH000Coding agentsKTPH001, turn off KTPH002Desktop notification when a coding agent needs a decision or finishes while you are not looking at its paneKTPH003 and save to disable korTTY's detected-agent notifications. Detection, the sidebar and the app badge remain available; configure those under KTPH004TerminalKTPH005 and see KTPH006Coding agentsKTPH007.

Notifications requested directly by terminal programs (OSC 9 / OSC 777) and long-running-command notifications have their own switches on this page. An agent running on a remote server uses the program-notification channel because korTTY only detects agents in local shells. Turn off the corresponding switch too if you want to mute that channel.

Long-running-command notifications and their minimum-runtime field are unavailable while shell integration is off under KTPH000TerminalKTPH001. Re-enabling shell integration makes the controls available again.
KTPH000Monitor for Silence reports after:KTPH001 sets the delay for tabs watched through their context menu. Activity and silence monitoring are enabled per tab, not by a global notification switch.
An KTPH000enterprise policyKTPH001 can disable desktop notifications and lock the notification switches. Tab attention marks remain visible inside korTTY.
See KTPH000Terminal notificationsKTPH001 for event handling and notification clicks, and KTPH002Coding agentsKTPH003 for the detected-agent notification behavior.

A program that rings the terminal bell in a tab you are not looking at always marks that tab with 🔔 until you look at it; this needs no setting. KTPH001Desktop notification when the bell rings in a tab you are not looking atKTPH002 adds a desktop notification titled KTPH000 and the tab's name, at most one per pane every 10 seconds. It is off by default because shells ring the bell on every failed Tab completion, and a pane with a detected coding agent gets none while the coding-agent notifications are on. The setting is read on every bell, so a change applies to open tabs as soon as you save.

In a shell set up for shell integration, a command that ran at least KTPH000Minimum command runtime:KTPH001 (30 seconds by default) and finishes in a tab you are not looking at marks that tab with 🔔 too, and KTPH002Desktop notification when a long-running command finishes in a tab you are not looking atKTPH003, on by default, adds a desktop notification saying how the command ended and how long it ran, never the command itself, at most one per tab every 10 seconds. Commands of korTTY's AI Agent never notify. Both are greyed out while KTPH004Use the command marks of shells set up for shell integration (OSC 133)KTPH005 is off, and both are read on every finished command. See KTPH006Terminal notificationsKTPH007.

A program that asks for a desktop notification with OSC 9 or OSC 777, such as a coding agent on a server waiting for your answer, marks its tab with 🔔 too when you are not looking at it, and KTPH000Desktop notification when a program in a tab you are not looking at asks for one (OSC 9, OSC 777)KTPH001, on by default, shows the program's text below a title with the tab's name, cleaned of control and bidi characters and cut to 80 characters for the title and 200 for the text, at most one per pane every 5 seconds; what comes in between is dropped. A pane with a detected coding agent gets none while the coding-agent notifications are on. It needs no shell integration and is read on every request. See KTPH002Notifications from programsKTPH003.

KTPH000Desktop notification when an AI agent or AI swarm run in a tab you are not looking at finishes or waits for youKTPH001, on by default, covers korTTY's own AI Agent and AI Swarm: when a run in a tab you are not looking at waits for your approval or a password, finishes or stops without finishing, a desktop notification titled with the tab's name says so in one fixed sentence, never with the prompt, a command or output, at most one per tab and kind every 10 seconds. A terminal tab is marked with 🔔 either way. It is read on every event. See KTPH002AI agent and AI Swarm runsKTPH003.

KTPH000Monitor for Silence reports after:KTPH001 is how long a pane has to stay without output, after printing something, before a tab you watch with KTPH002Monitor for SilenceKTPH003 in its right-click menu is marked with 🔔 and shows a desktop notification, 30 seconds by default. The watch itself, like KTPH004Monitor for ActivityKTPH005, which reports new output after 10 seconds of quiet, is switched per tab, off until you switch it on, and never saved. The threshold is read every second, so a change applies to the watched tabs as soon as you save. See KTPH006Watching a tab for activity or silenceKTPH007.
